outline.title: Executive verdict
outline.summary: Aethelgard has a credible prototype foundation, but it is not yet an AAA-ready game. Frame the immediate decision around truthful depth and a device-tested 3D slice.

outline.title: Product identity
outline.summary: Position Aethelgard as a landscape anime-fantasy survival RPG with a two-layer Android prototype and Unreal production path.
outline.image_plan: /home/ubuntu/upload/search_images/Q6ivcCqHTkQI.jpg - Anime fantasy forest background matching product identity description

outline.title: The playable loop already connects
outline.summary: Show the current Android sequence: move, gather, craft, fight, gain XP, and complete The First Ember quest.

outline.title: Two-layer architecture
outline.summary: Contrast the deterministic Android contract prototype with the intended Unreal 3D production path.

outline.title: What is working
outline.summary: Highlight input, native module separation, progression testing, audio polish, and Compose inventory foundations.

outline.title: The critical gaps
outline.summary: Show the most important risks: 2D presentation, static enemy behavior, UI-only inventory, missing saves, hard-coded content, and no multiplayer authority.

outline.title: Readiness scorecard
outline.summary: Present the repository-grounded subjective scorecard: prototype loop and input are strongest; content, multiplayer, and overall AAA readiness are low.

outline.title: Priority order
outline.summary: Lay out the recommended sequence: freeze the contract, build the Unreal 3D slice, make progression authoritative, complete combat, reduce HUD density, then scale content and co-op.

outline.title: Milestones and exit evidence
outline.summary: Map M1 through M5 to concrete proof: device captures, frame-time, save round-trip, combat depth, and four-client authority tests.

outline.title: Immediate decision
outline.summary: Close with the recommendation to start the device-tested M1 Unreal slice and stop expanding placeholder surface area.
